Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

# QA Story 835: Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want to build quotes using per-room, per-square-foot, or hourly pricing models with my own rate card, so that I can quote new work quickly and profitably without an in-person walkthrough for every lead. (Research: no pricing model is clean and underpricing is the #1 owner mistake — pain-points §1.4)

## Acceptance criteria

- Owner builds a per-room quote
- Switching pricing model clears the other model's inputs
- Per-square-foot total computes from the rate card
- Owner quotes a phone lead without visiting the property
- Missing rate on the chosen model blocks finalizing
- Rate-card change does not alter an already-sent quote

## Findings and done signal

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__create_issue` **as you find it** — not
written into a markdown file. Capture the title, severity, scope, and a
short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

    mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result(
      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]
    )

Discipline:

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just
  disappeared when your session ended — there's nowhere else for it to
  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

# QA Story Workflow

The `qa_story` agent task is a per-story QA cycle: write a brief, then execute
it against the running app. The project-wide QA plan
(`.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md`) is a prerequisite — produced upstream by
`qa_setup`, not written here.

QA completion is recorded by a DB-backed attempt via `submit_qa_result`. There
is no result.md file in the loop. Findings are filed via `create_issue` as
they're uncovered and linked into the attempt by id.

## Phase 1: Testing brief

**Artifact:** `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md`

The brief is the concrete plan for testing this story — which tools to use,
how to authenticate, what scenarios to test, and what to assert.

Procedure:

1. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for App Overview, Tools Registry,
   auth strategy, and Seed Strategy.
2. Run seed scripts to verify setup works for this story.
3. If this story needs additional seeds or plan updates, make them now
   and update plan.md (don't fork into a story-specific plan).
4. Read the BDD spec files listed in the prompt. They have selectors,
   test data, and assertions.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source and
   spec to understand the feature.
6. Write the brief to `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` matching
   the `qa_story_brief` document spec from the prompt.

## Phase 2: Execute tests

There is no `result.md` artifact in this phase. Findings flow through
`create_issue` as you discover them; the run ends with one call to
`submit_qa_result`.

### Tool rules — pick by Phoenix pipeline, not by guess

- **UI / LiveView (`:browser` pipeline):** MCP browser tools only.
  Navigate, click, type, screenshot. Log in via the browser (credentials
  and login steps are in the plan).
- **API endpoints (`:api` pipeline):** `curl` with API key headers.
  ALWAYS single-line commands. Use
  `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` for API-key auth.
- **NEVER** use curl with session cookies or CSRF tokens for
  browser-authenticated routes. If a route is behind
  `:require_authenticated_user`, test it with MCP browser tools.

### Testing approach

- Capture a screenshot at each key state (initial load, after
  interactions, success/error states). Save to
  `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/screenshots/`. Screenshots are evidence
  and remain valuable — attach the path in the issue description for
  any finding that ships a screenshot.
- After scripted scenarios, explore freely: unexpected inputs, edge
  cases, empty states, anything that feels off.
- Reference existing scripts in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/` by path
  rather than inlining shell commands.

### Filing findings

The moment you observe something wrong — a broken UI, a 500, a missing
feature, an unexpected behavior — call `create_issue` and hold the
returned id. Don't accumulate findings in a notepad. Don't write them
into a markdown file. The DB issue is the canonical record.

- `title` — short, scannable.
- `severity` — critical / high / medium / low / info.
- `scope` — `app` for app-under-development bugs; `qa` for QA infrastructure
  problems; `docs` for docs gaps; (`framework` is a server-side concept and
  not selectable from the local list_issues filter, but `create_issue`
  itself supports it for harness issues).
- `story_id` — the story this finding relates to, when relevant.
- `description` — the reproduction, the expected vs actual, file paths,
  and any screenshot or evidence path.

If a finding is a duplicate of an existing issue (you'll see them in the
prompt's "Existing Issues" section), don't refile.

### Procedure

1. Read the brief at `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` for the
   complete plan.
2. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for auth strategy and seed commands.
3. Read `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling.md` and `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/`
   for tool usage patterns.
4. Run seed scripts to set up test data.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source to
   understand implementation details.
6. Execute each test scenario from the brief.
7. Capture screenshots at key states (save to the screenshots directory).
8. For every finding, call `create_issue` immediately and remember the id.
9. If you find a gap in the plan or the brief, fix it in-flight — update
   `plan.md` or `brief.md` rather than working around the gap.
10. Call `submit_qa_result` once at the end with `status`, the structured
    `scenarios` list, and the full `issue_ids` list. Then stop the session.

## What the evaluator does when you stop

The evaluator runs a thin check chain:

1. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` exists with required sections.
   (If missing, returns invalid pointing at `qa_setup`.)
2. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` exists and parses.
3. Checks whether a DB-backed pass attempt exists via
   `CodeMySpec.Qa.qa_complete?/2`. If yes, the requirement is satisfied
   and the session ends.
4. If no DB attempt exists but the brief is valid, feedback is returned
   demanding a `submit_qa_result` call. The requirement does NOT satisfy
   off a brief alone.

## The submit_qa_result contract

```
submit_qa_result(
  task_id: <task_id from start_task>,
  status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
  scenarios: [
    %{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."},
    ...
  ],
  issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue this run>]
)
```

Rules:

- `status: "pass"` with `issue_ids: []` is allowed — clean pass, nothing to
  file.
- `status: "partial"` or `"fail"` with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected** by
  the tool. File the findings first.
- Only `status: "pass"` satisfies the `qa_complete` requirement. Other
  statuses record an audit row but leave the requirement open.
- Resubmitting on the same `task_id` is allowed — each call creates a new
  attempt; the latest is canonical.

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

## Seed data scripts (.exs)

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

### Reference script: `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`

```elixir
# priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates a complete QA test dataset.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
#
# Usage: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs

alias MyApp.{Accounts, Repo}
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

# --- Helper ---
defmodule QaSeed do
  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")
user = case Accounts.get_user_by_email("qa@example.com") do
  nil ->
    {:ok, user} = Accounts.register_user(%{email: "qa@example.com"})
    {:ok, {user, _}} = Accounts.update_user_password(user, %{password: "hello world!"})
```

## Smoke test scripts

For hitting every route and checking for 500s:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${APP_URL:-http://localhost:4000}"
FAIL=0

smoke() {
  local path="$1"
  local expected="${2:-200}"

  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE_URL$path")

  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "$expected" ]; then
    echo "  PASS GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE"
  else
    echo "  FAIL GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE (expected $expected)"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

# Public routes
smoke "/"
smoke "/users/log-in"
smoke "/users/register"

# Authenticated routes should redirect to login
smoke "/accounts" 302

exit $FAIL
```

- Accept 302 as valid for auth-protected routes when not logged in

- Use `mix phx.routes` output to build the route list

### Login page structure

The `/users/log-in` page renders **two separate forms** side by side:
- `#login_form_magic` — email-only form that sends a magic link
- `#login_form_password` — email + password form that submits via `POST /users/log-in`

The password form is often **below the viewport fold** because it comes after the magic link form. You must scroll it into view before interacting, or interaction tools will timeout waiting for the element to be actionable.

### Re-authentication mode

When a user has an existing session (e.g., session expired but cookie remains), Phoenix renders the login page in re-auth mode where the email field has a `readonly` attribute. Detect this and skip the email field:

```
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('#login_form_password_email')?.hasAttribute('readonly') ?? false")
```

If the result is `true`, skip the email fill step.

### Reference login sequence (MCP tools)

```

# 2. CRITICAL: scroll password form into view — it's below the magic link form
browser_scroll_into_view(selector: "#login_form_password")

# 3. Check for re-auth mode (readonly email field)
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('#login_form_password_email')?.hasAttribute('readonly') ?? false")
# If false, fill email:
browser_fill(selector: "#login_form_password_email", text: "qa@example.com")

# 4. Fill password
browser_fill(selector: "#user_password", text: "hello world!")

# 5. Click "Log in and stay logged in"
browser_click(selector: "#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']")

# 6. Wait for page to load after redirect
browser_wait(selector: "body", timeout: 5000)
```

### Reference logout sequence (MCP tools)

Phoenix logout uses a `<a href="/users/log-out" data-method="delete">` link. Phoenix JS intercepts the click and issues a DELETE request. Just click the link:

```
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/")
browser_click(selector: "a[href='/users/log-out']")
```

### User switching

To test multi-user scenarios, log out first then log in as a different user using the login sequence above with different credentials.

`phx.gen.auth` requires email confirmation before password login works. Seeds must confirm users programmatically:

```elixir

# Confirm via magic link token (bypasses email)
{token, user_token} = UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
Repo.insert!(user_token)
{:ok, {confirmed_user, _}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

# Set password after confirmation (magic link clears tokens)
{:ok, {final_user, _}} = Users.update_user_password(confirmed_user, %{password: password})
```

### Core workflow

Every browser automation follows this pattern:

1. **Launch**: `browser_launch` (once per session, if not already running)
2. **Navigate**: `browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000")`
3. **Map**: `browser_map` (get element refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
4. **Interact**: Use refs to click, fill, select — e.g. `browser_click(selector: "@e1")`
5. **Re-map**: After navigation or DOM changes, get fresh refs with `browser_map`

**Step 1: Log in once at the start of the QA session**
```
browser_launch(headless: true)
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/users/log-in")
browser_scroll_into_view(selector: "#login_form_password")
browser_fill(selector: "#login_form_password_email", text: "qa@example.com")
browser_fill(selector: "#user_password", text: "hello world!")
browser_click(selector: "#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/dashboard")
```

`phx.gen.auth` generates predictable form IDs: `login_form_password` for password login, `login_form_magic` for passwordless/magic-link login, `registration_form` for registration.

**Step 2: Browse freely**
```
# Read page content as text
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/dashboard")
browser_get_text()

# Take a screenshot for evidence
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/settings")
browser_screenshot(filename: "settings.png")

# Get raw HTML when you need to inspect DOM structure
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/items")
browser_get_html()
```

### Verifying page content

```
# Read all page text
browser_get_text()

# Read text within a specific element
browser_get_text(selector: "h1")
browser_get_text(selector: ".flash-message")

# Count elements
browser_count(selector: ".item")

# Check element state
browser_is_visible(selector: ".modal")
browser_is_enabled(selector: "button[type=submit]")
browser_get_value(selector: "input[name=email]")
browser_get_attribute(selector: "a", attribute: "href")

# Programmatic checks via JS
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('h1')?.textContent")
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelectorAll('.item').length")
```

### Interacting with LiveView pages

LiveView pages work like any other page with Vibium MCP. After interactions that trigger server-side changes, use explicit waits:

```

browser_wait_for_text(text: "deleted")

# Submit a LiveView form
browser_fill(selector: "#item_name", text: "Test Item")
browser_click(selector: "button[type=submit]")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")

# Trigger a phx-change event (e.g., select dropdown)
browser_select(selector: "select[name='filter']", value: "active")

# Wait for LiveView to reconnect after navigation
browser_wait(selector: "[data-phx-session]", state: "attached")
```

### Filling and submitting forms

Use `browser_map` to discover form fields, then `browser_fill` to set values:

```

browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/items/new")
browser_map(selector: "form")
# Map output shows: @e1 [input] name="item[name]", @e2 [textarea] name="item[description]", @e3 [button] "Save"
browser_fill(selector: "@e1", text: "Test Item")
browser_fill(selector: "@e2", text: "Created by QA")
browser_click(selector: "@e3")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")
```

Use `browser_fill` to replace a field's value (clears first), `browser_type` to append to existing value.

### Semantic element discovery

Find elements without CSS selectors:
```
browser_find(text: "Sign In")           # by visible text
browser_find(label: "Email")            # by form label
browser_find(placeholder: "Search...")  # by placeholder
browser_find(testid: "submit-btn")      # by data-testid
browser_find(role: "button")            # by ARIA role
browser_find(alt: "Logo")              # by alt attribute
browser_click(selector: "@e1")          # click whatever was found
```

### Screenshots as evidence

Always take screenshots for QA evidence, especially for visual checks:
```
browser_screenshot(filename: "qa_dashboard.png")
browser_screenshot(filename: "annotated.png", annotate: true)
browser_screenshot(filename: "full.png", fullPage: true)
```

### Advanced interactions

```
# File upload
browser_upload(selector: "input[type=file]", files: ["./document.pdf"])

# Multi-tab workflows (OAuth redirects, popups)
browser_new_tab(url: "http://external-provider.com/authorize")
browser_click(selector: "#authorize-button")
browser_switch_tab(index: 0)

# Drag-and-drop
browser_drag(source: ".draggable", target: ".drop-target")

# Keyboard shortcuts
browser_keys(keys: "Control+a")
browser_press(key: "Enter", selector: "#search-input")

# Hover interactions
browser_hover(selector: ".menu-trigger")

# Viewport testing
browser_set_viewport(width: 375, height: 812)  # iPhone viewport
browser_screenshot(filename: "mobile.png")
```

### Key tools by category

| Category | MCP Tools |
|----------|-----------|
| Navigate | `browser_navigate`, `browser_back`, `browser_forward`, `browser_reload`, `browser_get_url`, `browser_get_title` |
| Discover | `browser_map`, `browser_diff_map`, `browser_find`, `browser_find_all`, `browser_count` |
| Read | `browser_get_text`, `browser_get_html`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_a11y_tree`, `browser_evaluate` |
| Interact | `browser_click`, `browser_dblclick`, `browser_fill`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_hover`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_keys`, `browser_select`, `browser_check`, `browser_uncheck` |
| Forms | `browser_fill` (clear+type), `browser_type` (append), `browser_select`, `browser_upload`, `browser_get_value` |
| State | `browser_is_visible`, `browser_is_enabled`, `browser_is_checked`, `browser_get_attribute`, `browser_get_value` |
| Wait | `browser_wait`, `browser_wait_for_url`, `browser_wait_for_text`, `browser_wait_for_load`, `browser_wait_for_fn` |
| Tabs | `browser_list_tabs`, `browser_new_tab`, `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_close_tab` |
| Auth | `browser_storage_state`, `browser_restore_storage`, `browser_get_cookies`, `browser_set_cookie`, `browser_delete_cookies` |
| Capture | `browser_screenshot` (`fullPage`, `annotate`), `browser_pdf` |
| Session | `browser_launch`, `browser_quit` |

### Troubleshooting

- **Stale refs?** Always re-map after navigation or DOM changes — refs are invalidated on page change
- **Element not actionable?** All interaction tools auto-wait, but use explicit `browser_wait` for dynamically loaded content
- **Need full tool reference?** See `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/vibium_reference.md`

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

```elixir
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")

    user
  user ->

    user
end

# --- 2. More entities using context functions ---

account = QaSeed.find_or_create(MyApp.Accounts.Account, :name, "QA Account", fn ->
  Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "QA Account"})
end)

# ... more entities, each using context functions with scope

# --- Summary ---
IO.puts("""

==========================================
 QA Seed Data — Credentials
==========================================

Email:    qa@example.com
Password: hello world!
URL:      http://localhost:4000/users/log-in
""")
```

```
browser_click(selector: "button[type=submit]")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")

# Trigger a phx-change event (e.g., select dropdown)
browser_select(selector: "select[name='filter']", value: "active")

# Wait for LiveView to reconnect after navigation
browser_wait(selector: "[data-phx-session]", state: "attached")
```

### Filling and submitting forms

Use `browser_map` to discover form fields, then `browser_fill` to set values:

```
# Create a new item via form
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/items/new")
browser_map(selector: "form")
# Map output shows: @e1 [input] name="item[name]", @e2 [textarea] name="item[description]", @e3 [button] "Save"
browser_fill(selector: "@e1", text: "Test Item")
browser_fill(selector: "@e2", text: "Created by QA")
browser_click(selector: "@e3")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")
```

Use `browser_fill` to replace a field's value (clears first), `browser_type` to append to existing value.

### Semantic element discovery

Find elements without CSS selectors:
```
browser_find(text: "Sign In")           # by visible text
browser_find(label: "Email")            # by form label
browser_find(placeholder: "Search...")  # by placeholder
browser_find(testid: "submit-btn")      # by data-testid
browser_find(role: "button")            # by ARIA role
browser_find(alt: "Logo")              # by alt attribute
browser_click(selector: "@e1")          # click whatever was found
```

### Screenshots as evidence

Always take screenshots for QA evidence, especially for visual checks:
```
browser_screenshot(filename: "qa_dashboard.png")
browser_screenshot(filename: "annotated.png", annotate: true)
browser_screenshot(filename: "full.png", fullPage: true)
```

### Advanced interactions

```
# File upload
browser_upload(selector: "input[type=file]", files: ["./document.pdf"])

# Multi-tab workflows (OAuth redirects, popups)
browser_new_tab(url: "http://external-provider.com/authorize")
browser_click(selector: "#authorize-button")
browser_switch_tab(index: 0)

# Drag-and-drop
browser_drag(source: ".draggable", target: ".drop-target")

# Keyboard shortcuts
browser_keys(keys: "Control+a")
browser_press(key: "Enter", selector: "#search-input")

# Hover interactions
browser_hover(selector: ".menu-trigger")

# Viewport testing
browser_set_viewport(width: 375, height: 812)  # iPhone viewport
browser_screenshot(filename: "mobile.png")
```

### Key tools by category

| Category | MCP Tools |
|----------|-----------|
| Navigate | `browser_navigate`, `browser_back`, `browser_forward`, `browser_reload`, `browser_get_url`, `browser_get_title` |
| Discover | `browser_map`, `browser_diff_map`, `browser_find`, `browser_find_all`, `browser_count` |
| Read | `browser_get_text`, `browser_get_html`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_a11y_tree`, `browser_evaluate` |
| Interact | `browser_click`, `browser_dblclick`, `browser_fill`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_hover`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_keys`, `browser_select`, `browser_check`, `browser_uncheck` |
| Forms | `browser_fill` (clear+type), `browser_type` (append), `browser_select`, `browser_upload`, `browser_get_value` |
| State | `browser_is_visible`, `browser_is_enabled`, `browser_is_checked`, `browser_get_attribute`, `browser_get_value` |
| Wait | `browser_wait`, `browser_wait_for_url`, `browser_wait_for_text`, `browser_wait_for_load`, `browser_wait_for_fn` |
| Tabs | `browser_list_tabs`, `browser_new_tab`, `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_close_tab` |
| Auth | `browser_storage_state`, `browser_restore_storage`, `browser_get_cookies`, `browser_set_cookie`, `browser_delete_cookies` |
| Capture | `browser_screenshot` (`fullPage`, `annotate`), `browser_pdf` |
| Session | `browser_launch`, `browser_quit` |

### Troubleshooting

- **Stale refs?** Always re-map after navigation or DOM changes — refs are invalidated on page change
- **Element not actionable?** All interaction tools auto-wait, but use explicit `browser_wait` for dynamically loaded content
- **Need full tool reference?** See `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/vibium_reference.md`

## Example Scripts

### Browser session auth (Vibium MCP — for UI/LiveView routes)

The agent calls MCP tools directly for login/logout/QA setup. See the "Reference login sequence" and "Reference logout sequence" sections above for the tool call patterns.

For QA session setup:
1. Run seeds via bash: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`
2. Launch browser: `browser_launch(headless: true)`
3. Log in using the login sequence above
4. Browse and test

### API auth (curl — for `/api/*` routes)
- `authenticated_curl_example.sh` — Wraps curl with the account's API key header. Looks up the key from the database or falls back to a known seed value. Use as a template for `authenticated_curl.sh`.

Copy and adapt the curl script for your project. The Vibium MCP tool call patterns above demonstrate browser lifecycle, seed runner integration, and `phx.gen.auth` login patterns.

  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7120 — Missing rate on the chosen model blocks finalizing:
  a quote cannot be finalized until every line item in the chosen model
  has a rate and the total is greater than zero.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "missing rate on the chosen model blocks finalizing" do
    scenario "finalizing is blocked and the owner is prompted to set the missing rate" do
      given_ "the owner's rate card has no rate configured for the hourly model", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner builds an hourly quote and tries to finalize it", context do
        context.quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "hourly", hours: 3})
        |> render_change()

        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> element("[data-test='send-quote-button']")
          |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "finalizing is blocked and the owner is prompted to set the missing rate before sending, preventing a zero-dollar quote",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='hours-input'][value='3']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='missing-rate-warning']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$0.00")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7122Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7122 — Rate-card change does not alter an already-sent
  quote: a sent quote captures the rates and amounts at the moment it
  was sent, so later rate-card edits never change it.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "rate-card change does not alter an already-sent quote" do
    scenario "the previously sent quote still shows its original total after rates rise" do
      given_ "the owner sent a quote totaling $200 using the current rate card", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='rate-card-form']", rate_card: %{per_sqft_rate_cents: 10})
        |> render_submit()

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{client_name: "Morgan Ruiz", pricing_model: "per_sqft", square_feet: 2000}
        )
        |> render_change()

        quote_live
        |> element("[data-test='send-quote-button']")
        |> render_click()

        sent_quote_path = assert_patch(quote_live)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{quote_live: quote_live, sent_quote_path: sent_quote_path})}
      end

      when_ "the owner later raises the rate card rates", context do
        {:ok, new_quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        new_quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='rate-card-form']", rate_card: %{per_sqft_rate_cents: 20})
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the previously sent quote still shows $200 and its line items are unchanged",
            context do
        {:ok, sent_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.sent_quote_path)

        assert html =~ "$200.00"
        assert has_element?(sent_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$200.00")
        refute has_element?(sent_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$400.00")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Qa Story Brief — 835: Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing

## Tool

web

## Auth

- Login URL: `http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in`
- Password form fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`
- Owner creds: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`
- Log in as the owner (this story is `persona:owner`). Success redirects to `/`.

## Seeds

- `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent) — creates owner `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test`,
  cleaner `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` (both password `qa password 1234`), and account
  "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co". No story-specific seeds needed — the rate card and quotes
  are created live during the session via `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder` at
  `/quotes/new`.

## What To Test

Builder page (`/quotes/new`) has two forms: `[data-test='rate-card-form']` (persists
immediately on submit) and `[data-test='quote-form']` (in-memory until sent, phx-change
triggers `validate`). Model-specific inputs (`room-bedroom-count-input`,
`room-bathroom-count-input`, `square-feet-input`, `hours-input`) only carry their
`data-test` attribute while their model is selected — the underlying `<input>` stays
mounted but inert otherwise, so absence of the `data-test` attribute (not the element)
is the signal to check.

- **Criterion 7112 — per-room quote:** On `/quotes/new`, select pricing model "Per room",
  enter bedroom/bathroom counts. Expect `room-bedroom-count-input` and
  `room-bathroom-count-input` visible/tagged; `square-feet-input` and `hours-input`
  absent (no `data-test`).
- **Criterion 7114 — switching model clears inputs:** Starting from a per-room quote with
  values entered, switch pricing model to "Hourly". Expect the per-room inputs to lose
  their `data-test` tag (or read blank/hidden) and `[data-test='quote-total']` to reset to
  `$0.00` (not a stale per-room total).
- **Criterion 7116 — per-sqft total from rate card:** Submit `[data-test='rate-card-form']`
  with per-sqft rate = 10 cents ($0.10/sqft). Then on the quote form select "Per square
  foot" and enter 2000 sqft. Expect `[data-test='quote-total']` = `$200.00`.
- **Criterion 7119 — phone lead, no site visit:** With a bedroom rate of $50.00 and
  bathroom rate of $30.00 saved on the rate card, fill client name + phone (no address
  needed), pick "Per room", 3 bedrooms / 1 bathroom, click
  `[data-test='send-quote-button']`. Expect a patch to `/quotes/:id`, status badge
  `[data-test='quote-status']` = "Sent", total `$180.00` (3×$50 + 1×$30), and no
  "Schedule a site visit" text anywhere on the page.
- **Criterion 7120 — missing rate blocks finalize:** With no hourly rate configured (fresh
  rate card, or explicitly blank the hourly rate field), select "Hourly", enter 3 hours,
  click `[data-test='send-quote-button']`. Expect it does NOT navigate/patch away —
  `[data-test='missing-rate-warning']` appears, `[data-test='quote-total']` stays
  `$0.00`, and the hours value (3) is preserved in the input.
- **Criterion 7122 — sent quote frozen against rate changes:** Send a per-sqft quote at
  $0.10/sqft × 2000 sqft = `$200.00` (per 7116). Note the resulting `/quotes/:id` path.
  Go back to `/quotes/new`, raise the per-sqft rate to $0.20, save the rate card. Revisit
  the earlier sent quote's URL. Expect it still reads `$200.00`, not `$400.00`.
- Exploratory: try leaving pricing model unselected and submitting; try negative/zero
  room counts; check the `/quotes` index lists sent quotes with correct totals.

## Result Path

`.code_my_spec/qa/835/` (screenshots in `.code_my_spec/qa/835/screenshots/`); the
canonical result is the `submit_qa_result` DB attempt + linked issues, not a file here.

## Setup Notes

The rate card and quote-draft are both plain LiveView socket assigns until
`send_quote` is clicked — nothing is persisted to Postgres before that point, so there's
no need to reset any rate-card row between scenarios beyond re-submitting the
rate-card form with new values. Money is stored/rendered in cents via
`CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents/1`, formatted as `$X.XX`.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7153Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7153 — Completing a job generates its invoice
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking a job complete generates its invoice" do
    scenario "completing a job generates its invoice" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to the cleaner", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an invoice for $150 appears in the owner's billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7157 — Card-on-file charge is declined

  The charge submission itself is covered by criterion 7154's spec;
  this spec's subject is how a decline response from the payment
  provider is handled, so the pending charge is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "handling a declined card-on-file charge" do
    scenario "card-on-file charge is declined" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "an invoice is set to auto-charge the card on file", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: true})
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: job.agreed_price,
            status: :charge_pending,
            stripe_payment_intent_id: "pi_test_declined_123"
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the payment provider declines the card", context do
        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => context.invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id,
              "metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => to_string(context.invoice.id)}
            }

          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()

        assert has_element?(invoice_live, "[data-test='send-payment-link-button']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

      end

        {:ok, _invoice_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        assert html =~ "Paid"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees it settled in the billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "Paid"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

the invoice it triggers) is the one path every job completes # through, rather than a second one this view would otherwise need # for the no-checklist case. defp load_checklist(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job checklist = case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do nil -> {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, []) checklist checklist -> checklist end assign(socket, :checklist, checklist) end defp load_time_state(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job entries = TimeTracking.list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job) last_resolved = entries |> Enum.filter(&TimeEntry.resolved?/1) |> List.last() socket |> assign(:open_entry, TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job)) |> assign(:elapsed_seconds, TimeTracking.elapsed_seconds(scope, job)) |> assign(:last_worked_seconds, last_resolved && Earnings.worked_seconds(last_resolved)) |> assign(:earnings_cents, TimeTracking.job_earnings_cents(scope, job)) end defp client_name(%{client: %{name: name}}) when is_binary(name), do: name defp client_name(%{property: %{client: %{name: name}}}) when is_binary(name), do: name defp client_name(_job), do: "Job" defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-H:%M") defp format_duration(nil), do: "0m" defp format_duration(seconds) do hours = div(seconds, 3600) minutes = div(rem(seconds, 3600), 60) "#{hours}h #{minutes}m" end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public payment-link pages: a client without a card on file reaches
  `/pay/:token` (the link `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show` sends) to
  pay an invoice directly, no login required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> render(conn, :show, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]

    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
      {:ok, updated} -> render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)
      {:error, _reason} -> render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  defp render_not_found(conn) do
    conn
    |> put_status(:not_found)
    |> render(:not_found)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public Stripe webhook endpoint (`POST /webhooks/stripe`) — the only
  place an invoice's payment status ever changes from a pending
  charge, per the payments-stripe ADR. Verification (real signature
  check in production, trusted as-is in test) happens inside
  `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1`, so this controller never
  branches on anything but its result.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def create(conn, _params) do
    case Billing.receive_webhook(conn) do
      {:ok, _result} ->
        json(conn, %{received: true})

      {:error, _reason} ->
        conn
        |> put_status(:bad_request)
        |> json(%{error: "invalid_signature"})
    end
  end
end

#!/bin/bash
# Verify Stripe credentials by fetching the account balance (read-only).
set -u

if [ -z "${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo '{"integration": "stripe", "status": "error", "error": "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set", "details": "export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or add it to .env"}'
  exit 1
fi

response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance -u "${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}:")
http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -1)

if [ "$http_code" = "200" ]; then
  echo '{"integration": "stripe", "status": "ok", "details": "fetched /v1/balance with secret key"}'
else
  body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d' | tr -d '\n' | head -c 200)
  echo "{\"integration\": \"stripe\", \"status\": \"error\", \"error\": \"HTTP ${http_code}\", \"details\": \"$(echo "$body" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')\"}"
  exit 1
fi

Completing the job also generates its invoice, when `CleanerCrm.Billing` is present — read defensively per the moduledoc note on `CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job/2` about that hook not existing yet everywhere it's called from. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|-------------------|----------|----------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope | | job | `Job.t()` | yes | the checklist's job (for billing) | | checklist | `Checklist.t()` | yes | the job's checklist, items preloaded | Notifies the parent LiveView with `send(self(), :job_completed)` once the job is marked complete, so it can reload the job and checklist. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quality` - `CleanerCrm.Billing` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Billing alias CleanerCrm.Quality alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""

Checklist

<.button :if={is_nil(@checklist.completed_at)} data-test="mark-complete-button" phx-click="mark_complete" phx-target={@myself} class="mt-3" > Finish Job
""" end @impl true def update(assigns, socket) do {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:rooms, Quality.group_by_room(assigns.checklist)) |> assign(:progress, Quality.progress(assigns.checklist)) |> assign_new(:incomplete, fn -> [] end)} end @impl true def handle_event("mark_complete", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope case Quality.complete_job(scope, socket.assigns.checklist) do {:ok, _completed} -> maybe_generate_invoice(scope, socket.assigns.job) send(self(), :job_completed) {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, [])} {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, incomplete)} end end def handle_event("skip", %{"item-id" => item_id}, socket) do item = Enum.find(socket.assigns.checklist.items, &(&1.id == item_id)) {:ok, _item} = Quality.skip_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, item, "Skipped by cleaner") send(self(), :checklist_changed) {:noreply, socket} end # Not every account has `CleanerCrm.Billing` wired to this hook yet # (see its moduledoc) — read defensively so this component never # needs to change again once it lands. defp maybe_generate_invoice(scope, job) do if Code.ensure_loaded?(Billing) and function_exported?(Billing, :generate_for_job, 2) do Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job) end end end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live do
  @moduledoc """
  Talks to the real Stripe API over `Req` and verifies webhook
  signatures per Stripe's documented scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over
  `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"`, compared against the `Stripe-Signature`
  header).

  Requires `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (see
  `.code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md`). Verifying the signature
  needs the exact raw request bytes, which normal body parsing
  discards — `CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader` stashes them into
  `conn.assigns[:raw_body]` for the webhook route specifically.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway

  @base_url "https://api.stripe.com/v1"

  @impl true
  def create_payment_intent(
        %{amount_cents: amount_cents, payment_method: payment_method} = params
      ) do
    body =
      %{
        "amount" => amount_cents,
        "currency" => "usd",
        "payment_method" => payment_method,
        "confirm" => true,
        "off_session" => Map.get(params, :off_session, false)
      }
      |> put_metadata(Map.get(params, :metadata, %{}))

    @base_url
    |> Kernel.<>("/payment_intents")
    |> Req.post(form: body, auth: {:bearer, secret_key()})
    |> handle_response()
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{status: status, body: %{"id" => id, "status" => stripe_status}}})
       when status in 200..299 do
    {:ok, %{id: id, status: stripe_status}}
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{body: %{"error" => error}}}), do: {:error, error}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}),
    do: {:error, %{"code" => "request_failed", "message" => inspect(reason)}}

  defp put_metadata(body, metadata) do
    Enum.reduce(metadata, body, fn {key, value}, acc ->
      Map.put(acc, "metadata[#{key}]", to_string(value))
    end)
  end

  @impl true
  def verify_webhook_event(conn) do
    with [signature_header] <- Plug.Conn.get_req_header(conn, "stripe-signature"),
         raw_body when is_binary(raw_body) <- conn.assigns[:raw_body],
         {:ok, timestamp, expected_signature} <- parse_signature_header(signature_header),
         true <- Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(sign(timestamp, raw_body), expected_signature) do
      {:ok, conn.params}
    else
      _ -> {:error, :invalid_signature}
    end
  end

  defp parse_signature_header(header) do
    parts =
      header
      |> String.split(",")
      |> Map.new(fn part ->
        case String.split(part, "=", parts: 2) do
          [key, value] -> {key, value}
          [key] -> {key, nil}
        end
      end)

    case parts do
      %{"t" => t, "v1" => v1} -> {:ok, t, v1}
      _ -> :error
    end
  end

  defp sign(timestamp, raw_body) do
    :hmac
    |> :crypto.mac(:sha256, webhook_secret(), "#{timestamp}.#{raw_body}")
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp secret_key,
    do: config() |> Keyword.get(:secret_key) || raise("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not configured")

  defp webhook_secret,
    do:
      config() |> Keyword.get(:webhook_secret) || raise("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured")

  defp config, do: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
end

def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(
               scope,
               job,
               Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))
             ) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{
         before_photo: before_photo,
         after_photo: after_photo
       }) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
