    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(
               scope,
               job,
               Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))
             ) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{
         before_photo: before_photo,
         after_photo: after_photo
       }) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))

  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.

            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do

      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]

        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })

# QA seed script — idempotent. Run with: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates two confirmed users with passwords (an owner and a cleaner) and
# one account (the cleaning company) owned by the owner. Prints credentials.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

ensure_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})

      # Confirm via the magic-link flow (same path a real user takes).
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

owner = ensure_user.("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test")
cleaner = ensure_user.("qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test")

owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

account =
  case Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope) do
    [account | _] ->
      account

    [] ->
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co"})
      account
  end

IO.puts("""

QA seed complete.

  Owner:   qa-owner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Cleaner: qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Account: #{account.name} (id: #{account.id})

  Log in at: http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in
""")

# Story 836 QA seed script — run with: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_836.exs
#
# Assumes priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs has already run (owner user + account
# exist). Creates:
#   - two clients + properties for driving job-completion -> invoice
#     flows through the UI (one with a card on file, one without)
#   - two invoices seeded directly in :charge_pending with a known
#     stripe_payment_intent_id, so the decline/success webhook paths
#     (criteria 7157/7158) can be exercised via curl without depending
#     on whether a real charge submission to Stripe succeeds first —
#     mirrors CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures' own sanctioned shortcut for
#     these two criteria.
#
# Not idempotent (creates fresh entities each run) — safe to re-run,
# just accumulates a few more QA rows each time.

[account | _] = Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope)
scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

client_card =
  {:ok, client} =
    Clients.create_client(scope, %{
      name: "QA Card Client 836",
      card_on_file: true,
      email: "qa-card-836@example.com",
      phone: "+15555550836"

  client

{:ok, property_card} =
  Clients.create_property(scope, %{client_id: client_card.id, service_address: "836 Card St"})

{:ok, client_nocard} =
  Clients.create_client(scope, %{
    name: "QA NoCard Client 836",
    card_on_file: false,
    email: "qa-nocard-836@example.com",
    phone: "+15555550837"
  })

{:ok, property_nocard} =
  Clients.create_property(scope, %{client_id: client_nocard.id, service_address: "837 NoCard Ave"})

# --- Pre-seeded charge_pending invoices for the webhook-decision specs ---

seed_pending_invoice = fn suffix, intent_id ->
  {:ok, job} =
    Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
      client_id: client_card.id,
      property_id: property_card.id,
      agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
      status: :completed,
      scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
      start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
      end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
    })

  {:ok, _checklist} =
    Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
      %{
        task: "Kitchen counters wiped down (#{suffix})",
        before_photo: "before_kitchen_#{suffix}.jpg",
        after_photo: "after_kitchen_#{suffix}.jpg"

      %{
        task: "Bathrooms sanitized (#{suffix})",
        before_photo: "before_bath_#{suffix}.jpg",
        after_photo: "after_bath_#{suffix}.jpg"

      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
    })

  invoice
end

input.content: # Qa Story Brief — 836: Invoice completed jobs and collect payment ## Tool web (LiveViews under `:browser` + `:require_authenticated_user`) for job completion and invoice pages; `curl` for the two public, unauthenticated surfaces — `/pay/:token` (`:public` pipeline) and `/webhooks/stripe` (`:webhook` pipeline). ## Auth - Login URL: `http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in`. Password form fields are namespaced per-form: use `#login_form_password_email` (NOT the generic `input[name="user[email]"]`, which matches the magic-link form first) and `#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']`. - Owner creds: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`. The owner is an account `:owner`, so `FieldLive.Job`'s office-staff check lets them open and complete ANY job, assigned or not — no cleaner login needed for this story. ## Seeds 1. `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (base owner/cleaner/account, idempotent). 2. `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_836.exs` (story-specific, not idempotent — re-run creates fresh rows) — creates: - **QA Card Client 836** (`card_on_file: true`) + property "836 Card St" - **QA NoCard Client 836** (`card_on_file: false`) + property "837 NoCard Ave" - Two invoices seeded directly in `:charge_pending`, each with a completed job carrying real proof-of-work (2 checklist items with before/after photos each), for the webhook-decision criteria: - **DECLINE test invoice** — `stripe_payment_intent_id: pi_qa_836_declined` - **SUCCESS test invoice** — `stripe_payment_intent_id: pi_qa_836_succeeded` Print the client/property ids and both invoice ids/uuids on completion — the tester needs the invoice UUIDs for the webhook curl calls (payload `data.object.metadata.invoice_id`) and can navigate to `/invoices` to find their `/invoices/:id` URLs directly rather than parsing output. ## What To Test - **Criterion 7153 — completing a job generates its invoice:** At `/schedule/jobs/new`, create a job against the "836 Card St" property (today's date, any start/end time, price $150.00, no cleaner). Submit navigates to `/schedule/jobs/:id` — note the id. Visit `/field/jobs/:id`, click `[data-test='mark-complete-button']` ("Finish Job" — the seeded checklist is empty so there's nothing to gate on). Expect the header badge to read "Complete". Visit `/invoices` and confirm a new row for "QA Card Client 836" / $150.00 appears. Repeat against "837 NoCard Ave" at a lower price (e.g. $90.00) for use in the payment-link scenario below — both rows should be visible on `/invoices` afterward. - **Criterion 7154 — auto-charge the card on file:** Open the invoice for QA Card Client 836. `[data-test='charge-card-button']` should be present (card on file, unpaid, no prior intent). Click it and record what actually happens — a move to "Charge Pending" status, or a flash error. This exercises the **real** `StripeGateway.Live` adapter (`config.exs` sets `adapter: Live` for every env except `:test`) — note the payment_method it submits is a synthetic placeholder string (`"card_on_file:"`, see `CleanerCrm.Billing`'s own moduledoc comment on this), not a real Stripe token, so document the actual provider response rather than assuming success. - **Criterion 7155 — client with no card on file pays via payment link:** Open the invoice for QA NoCard Client 836. Confirm NO `charge-card-button` renders (client has no card on file), but `[data-test='send-payment-link-button']` does (status unpaid). Click it, then read the `[data-test='payment-link']` anchor's `href` (a `/pay/:token` path). Via curl: `GET` that path and confirm it renders "Pay Invoice" and the correct amount; then `POST` it with `payment_method=pm_card_visa&save_card=true` and record the actual response — expected per spec is "Payment received" + a "save your card" mention, but this also goes through the real Stripe adapter, so confirm rather than assume. - **Criterion 7156 — invoice shows the job's proof-of-work:** Open either seeded webhook-test invoice (DECLINE or SUCCESS — both carry identical proof-of-work). Confirm the "Proof of Work" section lists both checklist item task names (e.g. "Kitchen counters wiped down (decline)") and that at least one `[data-test='proof-of-work-photo']` `` renders. Note: there is no in-app UI path today to populate a checklist with named tasks on a real job (see Setup Notes) — this criterion is only reachable via the seeded invoices, not the two jobs completed live in the 7153 scenario above (their checklists are empty). - **Criterion 7157 — card-on-file charge is declined:** First, on the DECLINE test invoice's page, confirm its starting state is "Charge Pending" (no charge/retry button contradiction). Then `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4100/webhooks/stripe` with header `Content-Type: application/json` and body `{"type":"payment_intent.payment_failed","data":{"object":{"id":"pi_qa_836_declined","metadata":{"invoice_id":""}}}}`. Record the HTTP status/body (the Live adapter's `verify_webhook_event` requires a valid `Stripe-Signature` header computed from `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — an unsigned curl payload may be rejected with 400 `invalid_signature`; this is itself worth confirming either way). If accepted, reload the invoice page and confirm status "Unpaid" plus both `[data-test='retry-charge-button']` and `[data-test='send-payment-link-button']`. - **Criterion 7158 — invoice marked paid on provider confirmation:** Same curl pattern against the SUCCESS test invoice, with `"type":"payment_intent.succeeded"` and `"id":"pi_qa_836_succeeded"`/its invoice uuid. If accepted, reload the invoice page and confirm status "Paid", and that `/invoices` shows it settled as "Paid" in the billing queue. ## Result Path `.code_my_spec/qa/836/` (screenshots in `.code_my_spec/qa/836/screenshots/`); canonical result is the `submit_qa_result` DB attempt + linked issues. ## Setup Notes `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job.load_checklist/1` always instantiates a job's checklist as `Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [])` (empty) rather than through `Quality.instantiate_checklist/3` against a `ChecklistTemplate` — and no route/LiveView anywhere manages `checklist_templates` or calls `instantiate_checklist/3` at all. In practice this means a checklist created through the real product today can never carry named tasks or photos, so criterion 7156 (proof-of-work on the invoice) can only be demonstrated by seeding a checklist directly (as `qa_seeds_836.exs` and the BDD fixtures both do), never by a real owner/cleaner working a job end-to-end. Worth a filed issue regardless of how the rest of the story's scenarios land. Per the payments-stripe ADR (see `CleanerCrm.Billing` moduledoc), an invoice's status only ever advances on a Stripe webhook confirmation — clicking "charge card" or paying via link never marks an invoice paid synchronously, only `:charge_pending`. Both the card-on-file charge and the payment-link charge run through `CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live` in this dev environment (only `config/test.exs` swaps in the in-memory `Test` adapter) — real outbound HTTPS calls to `api.stripe.com` using whatever `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` the running server process was started with (not necessarily present in the tester's own shell env — check with `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_stripe.sh` if results look like a missing-credential failure rather than a declined charge).

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

input.title: Jobs created via /schedule/jobs/new never get client_id set, breaking invoice client display and card-on-file charging
input.description:
The "New Job" form at /schedule/jobs/new (CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent) only ever submits `job[property_id]`, never `job[client_id]` — this is the ONLY way to create a job through the real product (per the Job schema's own moduledoc: "the schedule board's own job form always carries a property"). Nothing in Scheduling.create_job/Job.changeset derives client_id from property_id.

Downstream, CleanerCrm.Billing.list_invoices/1 and get_invoice!/2 preload `job: :client` only (never job: [property: :client]), and CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show's client_name/1 and card_on_file?/1 helpers read invoice.job.client directly. With client_id nil:
- The billing queue (/invoices) shows "—" instead of the client's name for every invoice from a real job.
- The invoice detail page shows "Invoice for —".
- can_charge_card?/2 always evaluates card_on_file?(nil) = false, so the "Charge card on file" button NEVER renders even when the actual client (reachable via job.property.client) has card_on_file: true — criterion 7154 (auto-charge) is completely unreachable for any job created the normal way.
- send_receipt/2 also silently no-ops (client nil has no email), so the criterion-7154 receipt email would never send even if a charge succeeded.

Repro: created a job at /schedule/jobs/new against property "836 Card St" (client QA Card Client 836, card_on_file: true). Resulting invoice showed "Invoice for —" and only a "Send payment link" button, no "Charge card on file" button. Manually patching the job's client_id via psql (UPDATE jobs SET client_id = ... WHERE id = ...) immediately fixed both the displayed name and the charge-card-button's appearance, confirming the missing client_id is the sole cause.

Expected: billing code should resolve the client via job.client || job.property.client (or the job form/changeset should populate client_id from the selected property), so invoices from real jobs always resolve a client for display, card-on-file eligibility, and receipts.

input.description:
config/config.exs sets `adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live` for every environment except :test (only config/test.exs swaps in the in-memory Test adapter). Confirmed two ways:
1. POST /pay/:token (public payment-link page, CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController.create/2 -> Billing.pay_via_link/2) returns a full 500 Internal Server Error to the paying client, with stack trace:

       lib/cleaner_crm/billing/stripe_gateway/live.ex:91: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live.secret_key/0
       lib/cleaner_crm/billing/stripe_gateway/live.ex:35: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live.create_payment_intent/1
       lib/cleaner_crm/billing.ex:116: CleanerCrm.Billing.pay_via_link/2
       lib/cleaner_crm_web/controllers/payment_controller.ex:34: CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController.submit_payment/3
   This means criterion 7155 (client with no card on file pays via payment link) is completely broken end-to-end in this environment — a real client hitting their payment link and submitting payment gets a raw 500 error page, not "Payment received."

2. Clicking "Charge card on file" on an invoice (InvoiceLive.Show handle_event("charge_card", ...) -> Billing.charge_card/2) goes through the identical create_payment_intent/secret_key code path, so it raises the same exception. Unlike the controller case, this crashes the LiveView process itself — the `{:error, _reason} -> put_flash(...)` branch in InvoiceLive.Show never runs (the process crashes before returning), so the owner sees no error message at all: the page just silently reloads to its pre-click state, with the invoice still Unpaid and no payment record created. Confirmed via psql: no row in `payments` and no status/intent change on the invoice after multiple clicks. This is a silent-failure UX problem layered on top of the missing-credential root cause — the owner has no way to know the charge attempt did anything at all.

Root cause is environment configuration, not app logic (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY absent for this server process — note the shell environment has a similarly-named but different var, STRIPE_SECRET, which may be a naming mismatch worth checking upstream). Regardless of the fix, this makes criteria 7154 and 7155 both fail as currently deployed/tested. Suggest either supplying STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (test-mode sk_test_ key) to this server process, or defaulting non-prod environments to the Test adapter the way config/test.exs already does.

input.title: POST /webhooks/stripe rejects unsigned test payloads (400 invalid_signature) — criteria 7157/7158 not exercisable via bare curl
input.description:
CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live.verify_webhook_event/1 requires a valid `Stripe-Signature` request header (HMAC-SHA256 over "{timestamp}.{raw body}" using STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) before it will trust any webhook payload. Since this dev/QA server runs the Live adapter (see the separate STRIPE_SECRET_KEY issue filed against this story), a plain curl POST with a hand-built JSON payload and no signature header is rejected outright:

  curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4100/webhooks/stripe -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"payment_intent.payment_failed","data":{"object":{"id":"pi_qa_836_declined","metadata":{"invoice_id":"<uuid>"}}}}'
  -> HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
  {"error":"invalid_signature"}

This confirms (contrary to the QA task's assumption that "POST /webhooks/stripe with test payload is acceptable via curl") that the decline (7157) and provider-confirmation (7158) transitions cannot be exercised via a bare curl payload against this environment's webhook endpoint — only against a build using the in-memory Test adapter (config/test.exs), which trusts conn.params as-is. To QA these two criteria against a live/dev server, either compute a real HMAC signature with the actual STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, use Stripe CLI's `stripe trigger`/`stripe listen --forward-to`, or point this environment at the Test adapter for QA sessions.

Not necessarily an app bug (the signature check is the correct security behavior for a real Stripe integration) — filing so the QA process/tooling assumption gets corrected rather than silently producing false passes.

input.title: No UI path ever populates a job's checklist with real tasks — proof-of-work (7156) unreachable through the live product
input.description:
CleanerCrm.Quality supports checklist templates (list_checklist_templates/1, create_checklist_template/2, instantiate_checklist/3), but CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job.load_checklist/1 — the only place a job's checklist is ever created in the live app — always calls `Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [])` (an empty item list), never `instantiate_checklist/3`. There is also no route or LiveView anywhere in the router for managing checklist_templates, and nothing calls instantiate_checklist/3 from any web-layer code (grepped lib/ to confirm).

Consequence: every job completed through the real product has a checklist with 0 items — no task names, no before/after photos possible (ChecklistItemComponent, which is what renders photo-upload zones, only renders per existing item; an empty checklist renders none). This means criterion 7156 (invoice shows the job's proof-of-work: completed checklist + before/after photos) can only ever be demonstrated by seeding a checklist directly via the context API (as this story's own BDD spex and my QA seed script both do) — a real owner/cleaner has no way to reach that state.

Verified the rendering itself is correct when a checklist does carry items (via a seeded invoice: checklist items "Kitchen counters wiped down (decline)" / "Bathrooms sanitized (decline)" and 4 [data-test='proof-of-work-photo'] images rendered correctly on /invoices/:id). The gap is specifically in reachability — checklist templates need to be wired into job/checklist creation and exposed via some management UI for this story's acceptance criterion to hold up as a real, usable feature rather than a fixture-only path.

# QA Story 837: Send automated appointment reminders to clients

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want automated, reliably-delivered appointment reminders (email/SMS) with confirm/reschedule actions, so that cancellations and lockouts drop and my route density holds. (Research: fragile reminder delivery is an unresolved incumbent complaint; missed appointments are the top client grievance — pain-points §1.1, §1.6)

## Acceptance criteria

- Reminder fires at the configured lead time
- Client who prefers SMS gets a text reminder
- Reminder includes confirm and reschedule actions
- Client confirms the appointment
- Client requests a reschedule
- SMS reminder is undeliverable and falls back to email

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just

  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

  drive — the spec cannot call `CleanerCrm.Notifications` directly
  (sealed boundary). The appointment is pinned to the exact
  lead-time boundary (24 hours from now) so any conforming
  implementation's periodic check has already fired the send by the

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story837.Criterion7189Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 837 — Send automated appointment reminders to clients
  Criterion 7189 — SMS reminder is undeliverable and falls back to email

  The reminder send is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.notification_fixture/4` (covered
  end-to-end by criteria 7183/7185); this spec's subject is the
  provider delivery-status callback and the fallback it triggers.
  External SMS delivery status arrives the same way Stripe's does in
  story 836 — a provider webhook, never a live Twilio call.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an undeliverable SMS reminder falls back to email and flags the owner" do
    scenario "SMS reminder is undeliverable and falls back to email" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client prefers SMS but has blocked the reminder sender's number", context do
        client =
          Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{
            phone: "+15555550199",
            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
            preferred_channel: :sms
          })

        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{status: :scheduled})

        notification =
          Fixtures.notification_fixture(context.scope, client, job, %{
            channel: :sms,
            provider_message_id: "sms_test_undelivered_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, notification: notification})}
      end

      when_ "the SMS reminder fails to deliver", context do
        payload = %{
          "MessageSid" => context.notification.provider_message_id,
          "MessageStatus" => "undelivered",
          "ErrorCode" => "30003"
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/twilio", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "the reminder falls back to the client's email", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner is flagged that the SMS did not reach the client", context do
        {:ok, _reminders_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/reminders")

        assert html =~ context.client.phone
        assert html =~ "undeliver"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Schedules reminder sends ahead of upcoming jobs.
4	
5	  Driven by Oban's cron plugin in production (see the
6	  background-jobs-oban ADR): `perform/1` runs on a schedule and calls
7	  `scan_and_send/1`, the pure entry point, so the same check can also
8	  be run synchronously — deterministic, no clock-waiting — right after
9	  a job is created.
10	
11	  Only accounts that have explicitly saved reminder settings
12	  (`CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive`) are scanned, so this never fires for
13	  an account that hasn't opted in.
14	  """
15	
16	  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications
17	
18	  import Ecto.Query
19	
20	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
21	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
22	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderSettings}
24	
25	  @impl Oban.Worker
26	  def perform(%Oban.Job{}) do
27	    scan_and_send()
28	    :ok
29	  end
30	
31	  @doc "Sends every reminder that's due right now, across every account with reminder settings."
32	  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
33	    ReminderSettings
34	    |> Repo.all()
35	    |> Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))
36	  end
37	
38	  defp send_for_account(
39	         %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id, lead_time_hours: lead_time_hours},
40	         now
41	       ) do
42	    account_id
43	    |> due_jobs()
44	    |> Enum.filter(&due_now?(&1, lead_time_hours, now))
45	    |> Enum.each(&send_reminder/1)
46	  end
47	
48	  defp due_jobs(account_id) do
49	    already_reminded =
50	      from n in Notification, where: n.job_id == parent_as(:job).id and n.kind == :reminder
51	
52	    from(j in Job,
53	      as: :job,
54	      where: j.account_id == ^account_id,
55	      where: j.status == :scheduled,
56	      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
57	      where: not exists(already_reminded),
58	      preload: [:client]
59	    )
60	    |> Repo.all()
61	  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler do
  @moduledoc """
  Schedules reminder sends ahead of upcoming jobs.

  Driven by Oban's cron plugin in production (see the
  background-jobs-oban ADR): `perform/1` runs on a schedule and calls
  `scan_and_send/1`, the pure entry point, so the same check can also
  be run synchronously — deterministic, no clock-waiting — right after
  a job is created.

  Only accounts that have explicitly saved reminder settings
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive`) are scanned, so this never fires for
  an account that hasn't opted in.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderSettings}

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{}) do
    scan_and_send()
    :ok
  end

  @doc "Sends every reminder that's due right now, across every account with reminder settings."
  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    ReminderSettings
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))
  end

  defp send_for_account(
         %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id, lead_time_hours: lead_time_hours},
         now
       ) do
    account_id
    |> due_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&due_now?(&1, lead_time_hours, now))
    |> Enum.each(&send_reminder/1)
  end

  defp due_jobs(account_id) do
    already_reminded =
      from n in Notification, where: n.job_id == parent_as(:job).id and n.kind == :reminder

    from(j in Job,
      as: :job,
      where: j.account_id == ^account_id,
      where: j.status == :scheduled,
      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
      where: not exists(already_reminded),
      preload: [:client]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp due_now?(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}, lead_time_hours, now) do
    with {:ok, start_at} <- DateTime.new(date, time, "Etc/UTC") do
      due_at = DateTime.add(start_at, -lead_time_hours * 3600, :second)
      DateTime.compare(due_at, now) != :gt and DateTime.compare(start_at, now) == :gt
    else
      _ -> false
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: %Client{preferred_channel: :sms, phone: phone}} = job)
       when is_binary(phone) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    body = reminder_sms_body(job, token)

    case Delivery.send_sms(phone, body) do
      {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}} ->
        insert_notification!(job, job.client, :sms, token, sid, DateTime.utc_now())

      {:error, _reason} ->
        send_email_reminder(job, job.client)
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: client} = job), do: send_email_reminder(job, client)

  defp send_email_reminder(job, client) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    insert_notification!(job, client, :email, token, nil, DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp reminder_sms_body(job, token) do
    "Cleaning appointment reminder for #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}. " <>
      "Confirm: #{reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")} " <>
      "Reschedule: #{reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")}"
  end

  defp insert_notification!(job, client, channel, token, provider_message_id, sent_at) do
    %Notification{account_id: job.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: channel,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      provider_message_id: provider_message_id,
      sent_at: sent_at
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio do
  @moduledoc """
  Sends SMS via the Twilio Messages REST API using `Req` directly —
  no `ex_twilio` dependency, per the sms-delivery ADR. Configured via
  `config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio,
  account_sid:, auth_token:, from_number:, status_callback_url:`.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery

  @impl true
  def send_sms(phone, body) do
    config = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, __MODULE__, [])
    account_sid = Keyword.fetch!(config, :account_sid)
    auth_token = Keyword.fetch!(config, :auth_token)
    from_number = Keyword.fetch!(config, :from_number)

    form =
      %{"To" => phone, "From" => from_number, "Body" => body}
      |> maybe_put_status_callback(config[:status_callback_url])

    [
      base_url: "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01",
      auth: {:basic, "#{account_sid}:#{auth_token}"}
    ]
    |> Req.new()
    |> Req.post(url: "/Accounts/#{account_sid}/Messages.json", form: form)
    |> handle_response()
  end

  defp maybe_put_status_callback(form, nil), do: form
  defp maybe_put_status_callback(form, url), do: Map.put(form, "StatusCallback", url)

  defp handle_response({:ok, %Req.Response{status: 201, body: %{"sid" => sid}}}),
    do: {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}}

  defp handle_response({:ok, %Req.Response{status: status, body: body}}),
    do: {:error, {status, body}}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}), do: {:error, reason}
end

@doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    case Repo.get_by(Notification, provider_message_id: sid) do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}

# Qa Story Brief — 837: Send automated appointment reminders to clients

## Tool

web for `/reminders` (settings + delivery log) and `/schedule` (board);
curl for the public, unauthenticated `/reminders/confirm/:token`,
`/reminders/reschedule/:token`, and `/webhooks/twilio` routes (plain
GET/POST controller actions, no session — token is the only auth).

## Auth

- Login URL: `http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in`. Use
  `#login_form_password_email` / `#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']`
  (the plain `input[name="user[email]"]` selector hits the magic-link
  form first).
- Owner creds: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`.
- The confirm/reschedule/webhook routes need no login at all — they're
  public, token-authenticated links a client reaches from their own
  reminder message.

## Seeds

1. `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (base owner/cleaner/account).
2. `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_837.exs` — creates, all with `client_id`
   set directly via `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2` (bypassing
   `/schedule/jobs/new`, which per story 836's filed issue 410ef0c3
   never sets `client_id` — `ReminderScheduler.due_jobs/1` filters
   `where: not is_nil(j.client_id)`, so a real UI-created job is
   invisible to the scanner regardless):
   - **QA Email Reminder 837** (preferred_channel: email) + a job
     scheduled exactly 24h from seed time (the lead-time boundary)
   - **QA SMS Reminder 837** (preferred_channel: sms, phone set) + a
     job scheduled exactly 24h from seed time
   - **QA Confirm 837** + a scheduled job + a seeded `:sent` reminder
     notification (token printed) for the confirm-action test
   - **QA Reschedule 837** + a scheduled job + a seeded `:sent`
     reminder notification (token printed) for the reschedule-action test
   - **QA Undeliverable 837** (preferred_channel: sms, phone + email
     both set) + a scheduled job + a seeded `:sent` SMS reminder
     notification with `provider_message_id: "sms_test_undelivered_837"`
     for the Twilio-webhook fallback test

   Prints every client/job/notification id and token — use them
   directly rather than re-deriving from the UI.

## What To Test

- **Criterion 7183 — reminder fires at the configured lead time:**
  At `/reminders`, submit `[data-test='reminder-settings-form']` with
  `settings[lead_time_hours]=24` (matches the seed's 24h-out jobs).
  Then run the scan deterministically:
  `mix run -e "CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()"` (mirrors
  what Oban's cron calls in production — see
  `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler` moduledoc; don't wait on
  Oban's actual cron timing in a QA session). Reload `/reminders` and
  confirm the delivery log (`[data-test='delivery-log']`) gained a row
  for QA Email Reminder 837's contact info with status "sent". Check
  `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` for the delivered email.
- **Criterion 7185 — client who prefers SMS gets a text reminder:**
  After the same scan run, check the delivery log row for QA SMS
  Reminder 837 — expect channel "SMS", not "Email". This exercises the
  real `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio` adapter (config.exs
  sets it for every env except `:test`) — if `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`/
  `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`/`TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER` aren't valid for this server
  process, `send_sms/2` will fail and the scheduler's own fallback
  (`ReminderScheduler.send_reminder/1`) silently sends email instead —
  note whichever actually happens rather than assuming success.
- **Criterion 7186 — reminder includes confirm and reschedule
  actions:** Open the delivered email for QA Email Reminder 837 in
  `/dev/mailbox` and confirm its body contains both an `href="…confirm…"`
  link and an `href="…reschedule…"` link.
- **Criterion 7187 — client confirms the appointment:** `curl` the
  printed confirm token's URL: `GET /reminders/confirm/:token` for QA
  Confirm 837's notification. Expect an HTML 200 response containing
  "Confirmed". Then check `/schedule` (the board) and confirm the row
  for that job (`[data-test='job-<job-id>']`) shows "Confirmed".
- **Criterion 7188 — client requests a reschedule:** `curl GET
  /reminders/reschedule/:token` for QA Reschedule 837's notification.
  Expect 200 containing "Reschedule requested". Confirm the board's row
  for that job shows "Needs reschedule".
- **Criterion 7189 — SMS reminder is undeliverable and falls back to
  email:** `curl -X POST /webhooks/twilio` with
  `Content-Type: application/json` and body
  `{"MessageSid":"sms_test_undelivered_837","MessageStatus":"undelivered","ErrorCode":"30003"}`
  for QA Undeliverable 837's seeded notification. Expect `{"ok":true}`
  (the controller always 200s). Then check `/dev/mailbox` for a new
  reminder email to QA Undeliverable 837's address, and `/reminders`'s
  delivery log for a row showing that client's phone with a status
  containing "undeliver".

## Result Path

`.code_my_spec/qa/837/` (screenshots in `.code_my_spec/qa/837/screenshots/`);
canonical result is the `submit_qa_result` DB attempt + linked issues.

## Setup Notes

Per story 836's own filed issue (410ef0c3), jobs created through the
real `/schedule/jobs/new` form never get `client_id` set — only
`property_id`. `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler.due_jobs/1`
filters `where: not is_nil(j.client_id)`, so this bug has a second,
more severe consequence for this story: **a job created the normal way
through the product is permanently invisible to the reminder scanner —
no reminder ever fires for it, silently, with no error anywhere.** Confirm
this directly if time allows: create one more job via `/schedule/jobs/new`
at the lead-time boundary, run the scan, and check it produced no
notification — expected to reproduce the gap and should be tied to the
same root cause rather than filed as a brand new one, though the
consequence (reminders entirely unreachable, not just a display
issue) may warrant flagging at higher severity under this story.

Twilio's webhook handler (`Notifications.handle_delivery_status/1`, used
by `/webhooks/twilio`) does not verify any request signature — unlike
Stripe's, a bare curl POST is expected to be accepted and processed.

owner = Users.get_user_by_email("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test") || raise "run qa_seeds.exs first"
owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
[account | _] = Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope)
scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

due_at = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
due_date = DateTime.to_date(due_at)
due_time = DateTime.to_time(due_at) |> Time.truncate(:second)

end_time =
  case Time.add(due_time, 2 * 3600, :second) do
    t when t > due_time -> t
    _ -> ~T[23:59:59]
  end

{:ok, client_email} =
  Clients.create_client(scope, %{
    name: "QA Email Reminder 837",

  })

  Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
    client_id: client_email.id,

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderNotifier do @moduledoc """ Builds and delivers the appointment reminder email via `CleanerCrm.Mailer` (Swoosh/Resend). input.description:
Running a per-story qa_story session (story 837, task f4779ca8-2255-4c10-b0af-40e16f581129) in a shared dev-env repo where three other "fix" agents were concurrently hot-editing app code (schedule/billing/quality files). My session's stop hook fired twice demanding I "fix these problems before stopping":

1. "compiler: lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex — this clause of defp office_staff?/1 is never used" — code I never touched; it was mid-edit by a concurrent fix agent and has since been resolved externally (confirmed via a file-changed system reminder showing office_staff?/1 merged into a single clause).
2. "exunit: test/cleaner_crm_web/live/quality_live/templates_verification_test.exs:85 — ArgumentError: no push or navigation command found within JS commands" — again, a file I never touched, in an area (quality) other agents were editing.

Per my qa_story task instructions, the QA agent must NOT edit app code and must NOT run dev-env `mix compile`/`mix test` (a separate finding from this same session: any `mix run` invocation recompiles and poisons the shared CodeReloader-backed dev server for everyone, so QA sessions are barred from running mix at all beyond seed scripts). This leaves no sanctioned way to satisfy a stop hook that gates session termination on project-wide compiler/exunit cleanliness — the QA agent can neither fix the flagged files (out of scope) nor verify/re-run the checks (barred from mix) nor wait it out cleanly (the hook re-fires with a new unrelated failure each time another agent's edit is mid-flight).

Suggest either: scoping the stop hook's compiler/exunit check to files the current session actually touched, allowing a QA-role session to acknowledge-and-continue past unrelated pre-existing failures, or having it tolerant of the known shared-dev-server multi-agent editing pattern this team is using.

input.title: Twilio send crashes the entire reminder scan with KeyError — SMS-preferring clients get no reminder at all, and it can starve other accounts' reminders in the same pass
input.description:
config/config.exs sets `:sms_delivery_adapter` to the real `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio` adapter for every environment except `:test`. But the Twilio credentials block in config/runtime.exs (account_sid/auth_token/from_number/status_callback_url) sits entirely inside `if config_env() == :prod do ... end` — so in `:dev` (and any non-prod env), `Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio, [])` returns `[]`, not even nil-valued keys.

`CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio.send_sms/2` reads this config with `Keyword.fetch!(config, :account_sid)`, which raises `KeyError` (not a graceful `{:error, reason}`) when the key is absent. Confirmed directly:

  mix run -e "CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()"
  ** (KeyError) key :account_sid not found in: []
      lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/delivery/twilio.ex:14: CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio.send_sms/2
      lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/reminder_scheduler.ex:77: CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler.send_reminder/1

Two distinct problems this causes:
1. `ReminderScheduler.send_reminder/1`'s own fallback (`case Delivery.send_sms(...) do {:ok,...} -> ...; {:error,_} -> send_email_reminder(...) end`) can never catch this, because `Keyword.fetch!` raises before returning any tuple. Confirmed via psql: the SMS-preferring client's due job got ZERO notification rows created — not SMS, not a fallback email, nothing. Criterion 7185 (SMS-preferring client gets a text reminder) therefore fails completely in this environment: the client receives no reminder of any kind, silently.
2. `ReminderScheduler.scan_and_send/1` calls `Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))` across every account with reminder settings, with no rescue. An exception on ANY one client (this misconfiguration, or any other `send_sms` failure mode that isn't a normal HTTP error) aborts the entire `Enum.each` for every job enumerated after it — potentially starving other accounts' due reminders in the same scan pass of ever being sent. Confirmed empirically: in this run, an email-preferring client's due job happened to be enumerated before the crashing SMS one and got its reminder; had the order been reversed, it would not have.

Compare to story 836's analogous Stripe finding (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY also unconfigured in dev) — that one degrades gracefully per-request (500 to one caller). This one is worse: a single misconfigured/failing SMS send can silently block reminders for unrelated accounts and clients in the same batch, indefinitely (since the crashing job never gets a notification row, `due_jobs`' "already_reminded" exclusion never kicks in, so every future scan re-encounters and re-crashes on the same job).

Suggest: wrap `send_for_account`/`send_reminder` per-job in a rescue so one client's failure can't affect others, have `Twilio.send_sms/2` return `{:error, :not_configured}` instead of raising on missing config, and apply the Twilio credentials config outside the `:prod`-only guard (mirroring how Stripe's runtime.exs config already applies unconditionally) so dev/staging environments can actually configure and test it.

input.title: Reminder scanner silently never fires for jobs created via /schedule/jobs/new (same client_id gap as story 836, worse consequence here)
input.description:
Same root cause as story 836's issue 410ef0c3 (jobs created through the real `/schedule/jobs/new` form only ever get `property_id` set, never `client_id`), but with a distinct and more severe consequence for this story: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler.due_jobs/1` builds its query with `where: not is_nil(j.client_id)` (confirmed directly in the SQL logged by `mix run -e "CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()"`: `... AND (NOT (j0."client_id" IS NULL)) ...`).

Since every job created the normal way through the product has `client_id: nil` (per 410ef0c3), it is permanently invisible to the reminder scanner — regardless of lead-time configuration, regardless of how close the appointment is. No reminder ever fires, with no error anywhere, for any appointment scheduled the way the app's own UI creates them. This story's whole premise (automated, reliably-delivered reminders reducing missed appointments) is unreachable for real usage until the underlying client_id linkage is fixed.

Filing separately from 410ef0c3 (rather than only as a comment) because the blast radius differs materially: 410ef0c3 is a display/eligibility bug on invoices; this is a silent, total feature outage for the story's core automatic trigger. Both share the same fix (resolve/require client_id when a job is created against a property, or have every consumer — Billing AND Notifications — fall back to `job.property.client` when `job.client_id` is nil).

title: Twilio send crashes the entire reminder scan with KeyError — SMS-preferring clients get no reminder at all
severity: critical
scope: app
story_id: 837
description: config/config.exs sets :sms_delivery_adapter to the real Twilio adapter for every env except :test, but runtime.exs's Twilio credentials block (account_sid/auth_token/from_number/status_callback_url) sits entirely inside "if config_env() == :prod do...end" — so in :dev, Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio, []) returns []. Twilio.send_sms/2 uses Keyword.fetch!(config, :account_sid), which raises KeyError instead of returning {:error, reason}. Confirmed directly: `mix run -e "CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()"` → `** (KeyError) key :account_sid not found in: []` at lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/delivery/twilio.ex:14, called from reminder_scheduler.ex:77. Two consequences: (1) ReminderScheduler.send_reminder/1's own {:error,_} -> send_email_reminder fallback never runs because Keyword.fetch! raises before returning any tuple — confirmed via psql the SMS-preferring client's due job got ZERO notification rows (no SMS, no fallback email, nothing). Criterion 7185 fails completely. (2) scan_and_send/1's Enum.each over all due jobs has no rescue, so this exception aborts every job enumerated after it in the same pass, across accounts — confirmed empirically an email client processed before the crashing SMS one got its reminder, but ordering isn't guaranteed, so this can silently starve unrelated accounts' reminders too. Suggest: per-job rescue in the scanner, send_sms/2 returning {:error, :not_configured} instead of raising, and moving Twilio config outside the :prod-only guard (mirroring Stripe's runtime.exs, which is unconditional).

title: Reminder scanner silently never fires for jobs created via /schedule/jobs/new (same client_id gap as story 836, worse consequence here)
severity: high
scope: app
story_id: 837
description: Same root cause as story 836's issue 410ef0c3-daab-435d-b90f-6d52c1325880 (jobs created through /schedule/jobs/new only ever get property_id, never client_id) — but CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler.due_jobs/1 filters `where: not is_nil(j.client_id)` (confirmed in logged SQL from the mix run above: "AND (NOT (j0."client_id" IS NULL))"). Since every job created the normal way has client_id nil, it's permanently invisible to the reminder scanner — no reminder ever fires, no error, regardless of lead time or how close the appointment is. This story's whole premise (automated reminders reducing missed appointments) is unreachable for real usage until client_id linkage is fixed. Filing separately from 410ef0c3 because the blast radius differs materially: that one is a display/eligibility bug on invoices; this is a silent total feature outage for the story's core automatic trigger. Same underlying fix would resolve both.

content.text:
I've sent the team lead everything needed for a fresh-session courier to file the two remaining issues and submit story 837's result, plus handoff notes for the story 836 re-run. My work on this batch is complete:

**Story 835 (quotes): PASS** — all 6 criteria verified, no issues.

**Story 836 (invoicing/payment): FAIL** — 4 issues filed (client_id never linked from property, breaking invoice display and charge eligibility; Stripe credentials missing in dev crashing both charge paths; webhook signature blocking curl tests; no UI to populate checklist proof-of-work). Per the team lead, all four are now fixed and a re-run is queued for a fresh agent.

**Story 837 (reminders): PARTIAL** — 5 of 6 criteria pass (fires at lead time, confirm/reschedule links, confirm action, reschedule action, SMS-undeliverable-falls-back-to-email all verified working). One critical failure: Twilio's SMS send crashes with an unhandled `KeyError` in this environment rather than failing gracefully, so SMS-preferring clients get no reminder at all — and the crash can silently block other accounts' reminders in the same scan pass. Two issues were queued for the courier to file (that Twilio crash, plus the same client_id-linkage gap from 836 causing reminders to never fire for jobs created the normal way).

The session hit repeated infrastructure turbulence along the way — three separate CodeReloader crashes from concurrent fix-agent edits, and a CodeMySpec MCP server outage from a mid-session restart — each handled by pausing and escalating rather than self-medicating, per the team lead's protocol.
